questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some teachers are scientists. All scientists are doctors. All doctors are engineers. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are teachers. II. Some engineers are teachers. III. Some doctors are scientists.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some teachers are scientists.

All scientists are doctors.

All doctors are engineers.

Conclusions:

I. Some doctors are teachers.

II. Some engineers are teachers.

III. Some doctors are scientists.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some doctors are teachers → Follow (As, some teachers are scientists and all scientists are doctors. So, as whole scientists comes in doctors and have some part common with teachers therefore it is definitely true.)

II. Some engineers are teachers → Follow (As, some teachers are scientists, all scientists are doctors and all doctors are engineers. So, as whole scientists comes in doctors which whole comes in engineers and some part of scientists is common with teachers therefore it is definitely true.)

III. Some doctors are scientists → Follow (As, all scientists are doctors. So, as whole scientists comes in doctors therefore it is definitely true.)

Here, All conclusions follow.

Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some colours are rainbows. Some paints are rainbows. All rainbows are drawings. Conclusions: I. Some drawings are colours. II. All paints are drawings. III. Some drawings are rainbows.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some colours are rainbows.

Some paints are rainbows.

All rainbows are drawings.

Conclusions:

I. Some drawings are colours.

II. All paints are drawings.

III. Some drawings are rainbows.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some drawings are colours → Follow (As, some colours are rainbows and all rainbows are drawings. So, as whole rainbows comes in drawings and have some part common with colours therefore it is definitely true.)

II. All paints are drawings → Does not Follow (As, some paints are rainbows and all rainbows are drawings. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

III. Some drawings are rainbows → Follow (As, all rainbows are drawings. So, as whole rainbows comes in drawings and have some part common with colours therefore it is definitely true.)

Here, Only conclusions I and Ill follow.

questions.question: If ‘<’ means ‘−’, ‘!’ means ‘×’, ‘>’ means ‘+’ and ‘$’ means ‘÷’, then what is the value of the following expression? 183 > 39 $ 13 ! 6 < 26
questions.questionHtml:
If ‘<’ means ‘−’, ‘!’ means ‘×’, ‘>’ means ‘+’ and ‘$’ means ‘÷’, then what is the value of the following expression?

183 > 39 $ 13 ! 6 < 26
questions.solution:
After replacing the symbols with their meanings, we get :-

= 183 + 39 ÷ 13 × 6 - 26 

= 183 + 3 × 6 - 26

= 183 + 18 - 26

= 201 - 26

= 175

questions.question: Who introduced the Zamindari Settlement as a measure of land revenue administration?
questions.questionHtml: Who introduced the Zamindari Settlement as a measure of land revenue administration?
questions.solution: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Zamindari Settlement in 1793 as a measure of land revenue administration in British India. The Zamindari Settlement was a system of land revenue collection where the East India Company granted the zamindars (landlords) the right to collect revenue from the peasants in exchange for a fixed amount of revenue paid to the Company.

questions.solution: Schwann cells are the main glial cells in the PNS. They provide myelin sheath around the axons of neurons, which helps in faster conduction of nerve impulses.

questions.solution: The recommended daily intake of cholesterol for adults and children over four years of age, according to the guidelines provided by healthcare professionals, is RDA 300mg/day. Cholesterol is an essential component of cell membranes and is also involved in the production of hormones, vitamin D, and bile acids.

questions.solution: Microfinance refers to providing small loans to people who are unable to access traditional banking services, especially in developing countries. Muhammad Yunus pioneered this concept and founded Grameen Bank in Bangladesh in 1983.

questions.question: In ________, Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal.
questions.questionHtml: In ________, Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal.

questions.questionHtml: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 7. What is the measure of the largest angle of the triangle?

questions.question: A can finish a work in 60 days. He works at it for 15 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 48 days. In how much time can A and B working together finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a work in 60 days. He works at it for 15 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 48 days. In how much time can A and B working together finish the work?
questions.solution:
(A × 60) = (A × 15) + (B × 48) ⇒ (A × 45) = (B × 48) ⇒ A/B = 48/45 = 16/15

Total work = (A × 60) = 16 × 60 = 960 units

Total time taken by A and B working together = 960/(16 + 15) ⇒ 960/31

questions.questionHtml: A can do \(1 \over 3\) of a piece of work in 32 days, B can do \(37{1 \over 2}\)% of the same work in 24 days, while C can do 60% of the same work in 48 days. B and C together started and worked for x days. After x days, B left the work and A joined C and both completed the remaining work in (x + 8) days. If the ratio of the work done by (B + C) together to the work done by (A + C) together is 9 ∶ 11, then what fraction of the same work can be completed by C alone in 3.5x days?
questions.solution:
Efficiency Person Time Total work
10 A 96 960
15 B 64
12 C 80

⇒ (B + C) × x + (A + C) × (x + 8) = 960 ⇒ 27 × x + 22 × (x + 8) = 960 ⇒ 27x + 22x + 176 = 960 ⇒ 49x = 784 ⇒ x = 784/49 =  16 days

questions.question: If p + q + r = pqr = \(\rm {1 \over p} + {1 \over q} + {1 \over r} = 1\) , then find p 3 + q 3 + r 3 .
questions.questionHtml: If p + q + r = pqr = \(\rm {1 \over p} + {1 \over q} + {1 \over r} = 1\), then find p3 + q3 + r3.
questions.solution:
\(\rm {1 \over p} + {1 \over q} + {1 \over r} = 1\) ⇒ (qr + pr + pq)/pqr = 1 ⇒ (qr + pr + pq) = 1

p + q + r = 1 ⇒ (p + q + r)2 = 12 ⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 + 2 × (pq + qr + pr) = 1 ⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 + 2 × 1 = 1 ⇒ p2 + q2 + r2 = 1 - 2 = - 1

p3 + q3 + r3 = (p + q + r) ×  (p2 + q2 + r2 - pq - qr - pr) + 3pqr ⇒ 1 × (- 1 - 1) + 3 ⇒ - 2 + 3 = 1

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 99?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 99?
questions.solution:
Number = 60687 ⇒ The sum of digits = 6 + 0 + 6 + 8 + 7 = 27. 27 is divisible by 9. So the number is divisible by 9.

The sum of odd place digits = 6 + 6 + 7 = 19. The sum of even place digits = 0 + 8 = 8

Difference between the sum of odd and even place digits = 19 - 8 = 11 

11 is divisible by 11. So the number is divisible by 11. The number is also divisible by 99.

questions.questionHtml: A family income is Rs. 35,000 in a month. The family spends the income on various expenditures, viz., food, health, education, entertainment, and rent. questions.solution: Harming means causing damage or injury to someone or something. Example: The reckless driver caused a serious accident, harming several pedestrians.
